title: Rav Daniel bar Rav Ketina
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman says we always find “Rav Daniel bar Rav Ketina said that Rav said,” as in Moed Katan 8b and 12a, Chagigah 5b and Bava Kamma 97a. He likewise received from his father, who was a great man, as in Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 4:3: Rabbi Zeira sent and asked Rav Dimi son of Rav Ketina, “Did you hear from your father whether (the willow) requires a blessing?” After Rav’s death he sat before Rav Huna, as we find in Ketubot 97a: “Rav Daniel bar Rav Ketina said that Rav Huna said.” In Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 1:10 and 2, end of halakhah 1, he spoke in the name of Rav Chuna (he is Rav Huna); and in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, beginning of chapter 3, Daniel son of Rav Ketina in the name of Rabbi Assi (he is Rav Assi).

He is likewise mentioned in Gittin 86b, raising an objection to Rabbi Yochanan’s words, and in Chullin 62a he raises a difficulty against Rav Yehudah’s words, and Rabbi Zeira resolves his words (there it reads “Rechava said that Rav Yehudah said,” but in Dikdukei Soferim the word Rechava is absent). He was very pious, as related of him in Taanit 9b: he had a garden, and every day he would go and inspect it, saying, “This bed needs water and this one does not,” and rain would come and water wherever water was needed. In Berakhot 47a, according to the reading of the Rif and the Or Zarua, Hilkhot Seudah, siman 192, Rabbah bar bar Chana arranged his son’s marriage in the house of Rav Daniel bar Rav Ketina; Hyman’s received reading is Rav Shmuel son of Rav Ketina.

notes.text: The source’s Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah4:3 question names Rav Dimi, not Daniel; Hyman cites it for the father’s eminence. אזי is read as אזיל. Rav Huna and Rav Assi expansions are supported by Hyman’s full explicit parenthetical forms. The Rif/Or Zarua Daniel versus received Shmuel marriage reading is retained.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 4:3 reads Rabbi Daniel son of Rav Ketina, whereas Hyman’s quoted wording and retained current note say Dimi. This digital witness difference does not rewrite either the supplied quotation or the current note. Taanit 9b directly preserves Daniel’s garden and the separately watered beds; Rif/Or Zarua marriage and other exact-edition claims remain Hyman-attributed.
